title: At a fixed period, free sharp profiles reduce TIC 196904510 test errors by 0.27 to 7.78 percent in TESS sectors 92 and 93
abstract: We test whether a shifted and scaled sharp template from TESS sector 91 predicts TIC 196904510 in sectors 92 and 93. We set a 0.352714279-day period with sector 91 only. We fit alternate rotations and test on the other rotations. Free sharp harmonics reduce test mean squared error by 2.94 and 7.78 percent in corrected flux, and 0.27 and 2.08 percent in aperture flux. Linear background and pointing terms retain positive gains. The test uses 60 and 63 rotations. It shows imperfect transfer of the measured template at a fixed period. It does not reject every common latent waveform. Crowding, noisy template estimation, correlated cycles, phase drift and pipeline response limit the result. No planet, clump composition or new source is confirmed. We include code, exact input hashes, aggregate results and a figure. Raw observations remain external.

display.caption: Sharp profile transfer and error reduction on excluded rotations, at a fixed period. Bars are conditional cycle-bootstrap intervals.
